# a)
*include an output of three rows*

```{r a}
gra <- read.csv("ECN_VF1.csv")
btf <- read.csv("ECN_IB1.csv")

btf$SDATE <- as.Date(btf$SDATE, format = "%d-%b-%y")
btf$SYEAR  <- as.numeric(format(btf$SDATE, "%Y"))
btf <- subset(btf, FIELDNAME != "XX")

gra <- subset(gra, FIELDNAME == "VEG_SPEC")

btfCounts <- aggregate(VALUE ~ SITECODE + SYEAR,
                       data = btf,
                       sum)
names(btfCounts)[3] <- "BTFCOUNT"
graCount <- aggregate(VALUE ~ SITECODE + SYEAR,
                      data = gra,
                      FUN = function(x) length(unique(x)))
names(graCount)[3] <- "GRACOUNT"
df <- merge(btfCounts, graCount, by = c("SITECODE","SYEAR"))
head(df, 3)
```

# b)
*Limit: 100 words + 1 figure*

```{r b}
ggplot(df, aes(x = GRACOUNT, y = BTFCOUNT,
               colour = factor(SITECODE))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Number of Unique Fine-Grain Species",
       y = "Total Butterfly Count",
       colour = "Site Code",
       title = "Butterflies vs Fine-Grain Species")
```

It is clear that the recordings from the same site are bunched together as they are all contained in a section of the graph which is different from a different site. In addition, many sites have a very low amount of butterfly recordings, especially sites T03 and T11. In addition, generally, the higher the mean butterfly count, the higher the variance of butterfly count.

# c)
*Limit: 200 words + 5 figures + 1 table*

```{r c}
model <- lm(BTFCOUNT ~ GRACOUNT, data = df)
summary(model)

plot(df$GRACOUNT, df$BTFCOUNT)
abline(model,col="red")

cor(df$GRACOUNT, df$BTFCOUNT, use = "complete.obs")
```
The plot shows there is very weak correlation (~0.2) between the number of unique fine grain species and total annual butterfly count. This is likely affected by the very high butterfly counts in some sites. There is a huge amount of variance.

# d)
*Limit: 100 words + 12 figures + 12 tables*

```{r d}
list <- split(df, df$SITECODE)

models <- lapply(list, function(d) {
  lm(BTFCOUNT ~ GRACOUNT, data = d)
})

lapply(models, summary)

par(mfrow = c(2, 3))

for(site in names(list)) {
  d <- list[[site]]
  m <- models[[site]]
  
  plot(d$GRACOUNT, d$BTFCOUNT,
       main = paste("Site", site),
       xlab = "GRACOUNT",
       ylab = "BTFCOUNT")
  abline(m, col = "red")
}

sapply(list, function(d) {
  cor(d$GRACOUNT, d$BTFCOUNT, use = "complete.obs")
})
```
Some sites show a positive relationship while others show a negative one. Sites with the most positive correlation include T02 (~0.35) and T04 (~0.3) while T11 has some weak negative correlation (~-0.2). Some sites (T07, T08, T09) show no correlation at all while some (T05, T06, T10) also show very little. Site T12 only has 2 data points and is therefore not useful. Across each plot there is a huge amount of variance suggesting that fine grain diversity is one of many factors affecting butterfly population.
